Thanks Ben — forwarding to Legal + Privacy. Emily, thanks for the file. I'm capturing the asks below and enumerating what we need internally to respond.

Summary of customer asks (from their redline + email):
- Export control inventory for hosted infra and confirmation of controls on GPUs/storage in us-west-2.
- EEA -> U.S. transfer language: they want SCCs plus a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) to be accepted into our DPA; proposed language in redline (see attached).
- Subprocessor & data locality disclosures: update order form exhibit or provide a project-level subprocessor list and locations.

Internal evidence / items required from teams:
1) Export inventory (technical ops): a spreadsheet listing compute/storage endpoints, kdms used, and whether customer data leaves region (see template attached: export_control_inventory.xlsx).
2) SCC/TIA review (privacy counsel): confirm whether proposed TIA text is materially inconsistent with our standard SCC implementation; if so, propose counter-language.
3) Subprocessor & Order Form updates (contracts): confirm how we represent per-customer locality exceptions and whether we can commit to the requested exhibit.

Action owners & timeline:
- Monica (Legal/Privacy) — consolidate a redline response and proposed TIA countertext by Thu 5pm PT.
- Karthik (Security/Privacy) — review the SCC/TIA differences and recommend risk mitigations; also confirm whether we need an updated SCC attestation from infra by Thu 1pm PT.
- Lauren (Contracts) — update the msa-redline-tracker.csv with our positions and any procurement playbook language for exceptions; aim for Thu EOD.
- Ben (Sales) — coordinate the call with BioSignal and set expectation for follow-up Fri morning; share hubspot link after you schedule.

Subject: Re: BioSignal DPA redline (initial delivery)

Monica — quick technical/legal note from the TIA/SCCs perspective:
- Our standard SCC implementation already includes AES-256 at rest and TLS1.2+ in transit; that covers most of the customer "control" asks.
- The redline's proposed non-specified TIA paragraphs are broader: they ask for a data-transfer risk assessment that references export-control classification (ITAR/ EAR style wording). We generally don't provide export classification for customer payloads; that's an ops/counsel heavy lift.

Suggested positions (short):
1) Export inventory: we can provide a host-level inventory that lists regions, compute types, and whether HSM/KMS is region-bound. We cannot certify export classification of customer payloads — propose wording: "Provider will provide a technical inventory of hosted endpoints and cryptographic key locations; classification of customer content under export control laws remains customer's responsibility."
2) TIA / SCCs: Accept SCCs as baseline; for the TIA propose a mutual-acknowledgement clause that we will conduct a transfer impact analysis and share non-sensitive summary of mitigations, with any binding operational changes subject to commercial negotiation (i.e., cannot be unilateral).

I'll mark up the redline with the above and upload to the tracker. If Legal wants a call with Infra Ops to confirm the export inventory fields, we should schedule one tomorrow morning.

- Karthik
